title: Idempotent rewrite & structured-response bridge for OpenAI ChatCompletions compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Some enterprise customers rely on the legacy OpenAI ChatCompletions API surface but need Redwood runtime guarantees (low-latency streaming, reliable tool/function calling, and structured JSON outputs). Existing mappings are inconsistent for a subset of edge cases: chunked streaming frames that contain partial function call tokens, ambiguous role annotation when messages are rewritten, and request replay/idempotency mismatches between client retries and our internal fallback routing.

Scope: Implement a translation bridge that accepts ChatCompletions-style requests and produces equivalent Redwood internal request shapes while preserving: (1) streaming semantics (event/frame alignment and partial token emission), (2) tool/function semantics (deferred tool invocation, input marshaling, tool response reinsertion), (3) structured output signals (json_schema/structured output hints), and (4) idempotency mapping for retries and hedged write operations. This ticket covers the protocol/transport layer and server-side shims; SDK surface adapters are tracked separately.

Design decisions taken so far:
- Use a short-lived correlation token (cc_bridge_id) inserted as a header and mirrored into streamed frames. This is cheaper than full persistent correlation for most flows and enough to stitch retries together.
- Translate OpenAI's function_call: {name:"...", arguments:"partial-strings"} into an internal deferred-invocation envelope that marks call as "pending" until the final stream frame sets finished=true. We avoid eager tool invocation on partial frames.
- For structured outputs, we add an explicit structured_hint field derived from openai's 'function_call' and first system messages with schema links. The runtime will prefer to emit a structured result when structured_hint is present.
- Idempotency: map OpenAI 'user: message_id' and incoming idempotency_key (if present) -> internal idempotency token. If client doesn't provide token, the bridge generates one deterministically from (customer_id, conversation_id, canonical_prompt_hash).
- Backpressure & streaming: to preserve latency SLOs we will buffer partial frames up to a soft-limit (128KB) and flush intermediate delta frames with 'incomplete' markers so clients that expect partial tokens can render tokens immediately while the bridge keeps semantic bookkeeping.

Trade-offs considered:
- Persisting all in-flight state to DB for idempotency vs keeping ephemeral in-memory mapping: we chose ephemeral (LRU TTL=5m) for performance and fall back to a durable reconcile path for rare cross-host retries.
- Attempting to 'normalize' function call arguments into full JSON at the bridge level vs leaving parsing to the caller: normalize where feasible, but avoid changing unparseable inputs—emit a structured_error event instead so clients can decide.

Out-of-scope: SDK-specific compatibility layers, full multi-tenant audit log export, and deep linguistic normalization of tool responses.

Expected deliverables: design doc updates, implementation of bridge, unit + integration tests, basic benchmark for latency/extra-cost, and a canary rollout plan with telemetry gates.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge accepts OpenAI ChatCompletions request shape and returns Redwood-compatible response frames for normal generation flows
Streaming frames preserve token ordering and include cc_bridge_id header in each event
Function/tool calls are only executed after final function call frame (no eager invocation on partial frames)
Structured output hints cause runtime to emit structured JSON or a structured_error event when parsing fails
Idempotency token mapping prevents double-invocation for at least 95% of immediate client retries in e2e tests
Automated unit tests for the rewrite logic and streaming framing (>90% coverage for critical path)
Integration tests that simulate partial frame loss and client retry scenarios (passed in CI)
PR linked, design doc updated, and canary rollout plan documented with two telemetry gates (error-rate and 99th-p90 latency)
Documentation: add compatibility notes to API docs and update SDK migration guide stub

2025-02-12 Evan Cole (review): Noted concern about the TTL for ephemeral idempotency store. Suggested T=10m instead of 5m to reduce cross-host fallout. Recorded in design doc comments.
2025-02-13 Priya Nair (security): Reviewed header injection approach — SSO/SSO headers OK but redact tokens in logs. Added requirement to mask cc_bridge_id in user-facing traces.
2025-02-15 Marco Ruiz: adjusted prototype to only generate deterministic idempotency tokens when no client token is present. Added reconciliation job skeleton for rare double-invoke cases.

2025-02-17 QA notes: Integration harness simulated chunked streaming and partial frame loss. Observed one case where function args spanned >256KB and caused parser timeout — created follow-up ENG-314272 to handle large-arg streaming parser edge cases.
2025-02-18 Marco Ruiz: Preparing PR for main implementation (branch: eng/cc-bridge/idempotent-rewrite). Linking PR and canary plan below.
